title: Ex Vivo Assessment of Gut Barrier Function and Permeability
author: Amy Ehrlich
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yipfudn
materials: Prewarm the KRB solution in the 37°C waterbath.
On the File menu, select New Experiment
Values should be “area corrected” for real values.
Pull out O ² tubes then electrodes.

Sampling 1. After 25min of acquiring data, record base line Isc and G. 2. At time 0, collect 2x 100 µl from the serosal side and place in black plate or a 0.5 ml tube. (Store at 4°C). Replace with 200 ul Ringers+glucose 3. Remove 150 µl from the mucosal side and add sample of choice. ie: FITC-dextran 4000 (FD4) → 100 µl to mucosal side [small: goes through tight junction, paracellular] Stock solution: 10 mg/ml TdB Consultancy AB 1g Horseradish Peroxidase (HRP) (SIGMA) → 50 µl to mucosal side [big: goes through trancellular] Stock solution: 10 mg/ml 4. Collect 2x 100 µl from serosal side at desired time point (15, 30 or 60 min) and place in black plate or 0.5 ml tube. (Store at 4°C) 5. After 2 hours, Click on “stop” icon on the toolbar to stop data acquisition. 6. Turn off chamber, computer, and water bath. Taking tissues at different times 1. Selecting the tissues you are ready to use on the Experiment/Properties screen. Once you select the tissues on which to take data you will likely be required to take a reference. Do it. Start recording data. 2. Mount your next set of tissues and when ready, Stop the data acquisition and click on Experiment/Properties. Add the new tissues to the selection and press Save. You will have to Reference the new tissues (actually it will reference all of them again) and then start taking data again. This can all be done in a matter of about 10 seconds if you're organized. 3. Continue this until all tissues are mounted. Data Collection 1. Values should be “area corrected” for real values. 2. To export data to excel: Under Analyze Tools, select “Export Raw Data.” Select parameters under “data to export.” “Use experimental range” or “specify a range” for the test range. Select “export to excel.” Be sure that “area corrected values” is selected. Testing Tissue Viability Adding 10 uM forskolin to the chamber, which raises levels of cyclic AMP with resultant active net ion transport in viable tissue (as assessed by an increase in Isc). Add to both sides. Isc should increase and G should decrease Discard nonresponsive tissues.

HRP Assay Sodium Azide 0.1 % is made from 1 % stock (5ml into 45 ml of H20) To make 1%, use 1g Sodium Azide in 100ml H20 1. Mix 6 ml of Solution A and 44ml of Solution B. (3 into 22 for 1 plate) 2. Dissolve 1 tablet of o-dianisidine (Sigma Aldrich #D9154-50TAB) in 1ml of ddH ² O TOXIC!. Work under the fume hood when using o-dianisidine 3. Prepare standards for standard curve: Plates: LS1143 Elisa 96 Well from Central Services 4. Add 400 µl of the o-dianisidine solution to the Solution A + Solution B mix, (200 ul for 1 plate) 5. Add 5 µl (2.5ul) of 30% hydrogen peroxide to the Solution A + B mix. 6. Add 160 µl of this reaction solution per well. 7. Start the timer 10 minutes. 8. Stop the reaction with 100 µl of 0.1% Sodium Azide (NaN3) /well 9. Read absorbance at 450nm.

steps.title: Prepare Agar Tips
steps.instruction: Prepare 3% agar solution in Ringers or KRB solution (or 3M HCl) and fill electrode tips.

substeps.instruction: Combine 0.75g agar and 25 ml Ringers/KRB in a 50 ml conical tube.
Place the conical tube in a beaker filled halfway with dH2O and heat on a hot plate.
Degas the agar using an orange conical lid attached to a 30ml syringe to remove air bubbles until the center is clear.
Use a 1ml syringe (without needle) to suck up agar and backfill the tip until the lower quarter is filled.
Immediately backfill the tip with Ringers/KRB using a syringe with a filling needle.
Store tips in a tip box filled with Ringers/KRB at 4°C.

steps.title: Assemble Electrodes
steps.instruction: Attach the prepared tips to the electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Apply a thin film of silicone vacuum grease (stopcock grease) to the black rubber seal on the threaded shaft of the electrode.
Screw the backfilled tip onto the electrode, ensuring electrodes and tips remain in KRB solution to avoid drying.

steps.title: Collect Intestinal Tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest and prepare intestinal tissue for the chamber.

substeps.instruction: Collect intestinal tissue and remove contents without excessive scraping.
Immediately place tissue in low glucose DMEM medium.
Open the tissue and wash in KRB.

steps.title: Prepare and Calibrate Chambers
steps.instruction: Set up the Ussing chamber apparatus and calibrate the electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Prewarm KRB solution in a 37°C waterbath.
Start the 47°C circulating water bath (filled with dH2O) 20-30 minutes before calibration.
Power on the computer and clamp apparatus; set electrode sets to 'operate' for samples or 'test' for empty sets.
Verify Clamp Module settings: METER (Green light on 'V'), FUNCTION (All OFF), MODE (Green light on 'V'), OFFSET (All OFF), and KNOBS at zero.

Verify Pulse Generator Module settings: PULSE (All OFF), POLARITY (All ON), AMPLITUDE (Set to '3', red light on x1), PERIOD (20.0 seconds), DURATION (0.30 seconds), DC CLAMP LEVEL (All OFF), and KNOBS at zero.
Verify Master Control Module: All lights should be OFF.
Mount the chamber and sliders (white side left, transparent side right). Use 0.5cm² sliders for rats and 0.3 or 0.1cm² for mice. Tighten with the black knob.
Test black electrodes: Press OPEN; values should be between -3 and +3. Replace tip or electrode if outside this range.
Test white electrodes: Set METER light to red for 'I', press the black (Adj) button; values should be 51-54 (Ringers/Krebs tips) or 60-67 (3M KCl tips). Do not hold the black button too long.
Set electrodes in the chamber and add KRB solution, pulling electrodes slightly to remove bubbles.
Set METER light back to green for 'V'.
Calibrate black electrodes: Press offset and adjust knob A to '0' (use '+' offset if original value was negative, '-' if positive).
Calibrate white electrodes: Press black button and turn knob B to '0'.
Perform calibration with warmed medium to avoid temperature-induced voltage sensing errors.

steps.title: Prepare Solutions and Mount Tissue
steps.instruction: Prepare assay solutions and mount the intestinal tissue into the chamber.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Glucose and Mannitol solutions (fresh or stored at 4°C for <1 week) and warm in a 37°C waterbath.
Recalibrate electrodes and adjust offset.
Remove KRB from the chamber using a vacuum syringe and ensure the back of the chamber is completely dry.
Remove sliders and dry the inside of the chamber with a Kimwipe and tweezers.
Cut intestinal samples (1-2cm), avoiding Peyer patches.
Pinch tissue into the white part of the slider (mucosal side up) using the 8 pins for anchorage, then close with the transparent side.
Mount the slider in the chamber with the mucosal/lumenal side facing left and serosa facing right; tighten the knobs.
Open the 95% O2 / 5% CO2 gas tank and adjust flow through a water-filled beaker into the chambers.
Slowly add 2.5ml of Krebs+glucose to the serosal side (right) and 2.5ml of Krebs+mannitol to the mucosal side (left).
Aspirate any bubbles with a syringe. Confirm a negative current reading is present.

steps.title: Configure Data Acquisition Software
steps.instruction: Initialize the 'Acquire and Analyze' software and establish connection.

substeps.instruction: Launch 'Acquire and Analyze' software.
If connection errors occur: Restart computer, press F2 during boot, select 'onboard devices' -> 'LPT Port Mode' -> hardware 'EPP', then restart Windows.

steps.title: Acquire Experimental Data
steps.instruction: Set up the experiment in the software and record baseline data.

substeps.instruction: Select 'New Experiment' from the File menu, name the file, and save to the destination directory.
In 'Experiment Properties' under the 'Tissues' tab, select active tissues by left-clicking the colored squares.

Perform a zero reference reading: Select Acquire > Reference, press 'Master Override' and 'REM' on the clamp apparatus, and click 'reference' on the computer. Values must be < 0.1 (Yellow is acceptable, Red requires recalibration).
Start data acquisition by clicking the 'running man' icon.
Select individual chambers via 'remote' and set pulse speed (red-slow, yellow-medium, green-fast).
Configure Current graph: X axis Maj ticks = 60, Y axis Maj ticks = 20, Min = 80.
Configure Conductance graph: Y axis type to conductance, Maj ticks = 20, origin = 0; X axis same as current graph.
Allow the program to acquire data for 15 to 30 minutes before proceeding.

steps.title: Shut Down and Clean Up
steps.instruction: Deactivate the system and clean the components.

substeps.instruction: Turn off O2 and aspirate media from chambers.
Remove O2 tubes and electrodes.
Disassemble chambers and sliders; soak in soap and water.
Wash the chamber apparatus, chambers, and sliders with soap and water, followed by a final rinse with distilled water.
Briefly rinse the bottom of the tips (chamber-exposed part) with water.
For next-day setup: Dry chambers and backs completely, add dry inserts, attach electrodes, and fill with Ringers solution.
For weekly shutdown: Air dry all components. Detach tips and store in Ringers solution.

steps.title: Maintain Electrodes
steps.instruction: Clean and maintain the current driving and voltage measuring electrodes.

substeps.instruction: For white (current driving) electrodes: Remove buildup with a nail file or wet/dry sandpaper until shiny, soak in bleach until black, and rinse with water.
For black (voltage measuring) electrodes: Rinse with water and gently rub the sensing end on a paper towel (a small black spot should appear).

steps.title: Clean Tips
steps.instruction: Deep clean and dry the agar tips.

substeps.instruction: Soak old tips in warm water.
Use a syringe with water to push out old agar, then rinse with clean H2O.
Push water and then air through the tips.
Dry tips in an incubator completely before adding new agar.
